questions.question: What is subject-verb agreement?
options: The verb must agree with the object in number.
The subject must agree with the object.
The verb must agree with the subject in person and number.
The verb must always be singular.
questions.explanation: For a sentence to be grammatically correct, the main verb should agree with the subject in person and number.

questions.question: When the subject is singular, the verb should be:
questions.explanation: When the subject is singular, the verb should be singular.

questions.question: When the subject is plural, the verb is:
questions.explanation: When the subject is plural, the verb is also plural.

questions.question: In 'I speak Telugu, but Ajith speaks Kannada,' why do the verbs differ?
options: Because one is a collective noun
Because the subjects differ in person
questions.explanation: The verb takes different forms depending on whether the subject pronoun is in first, second, or third person.

questions.question: In 'Valli likes to build robots as a hobby,' why is the verb 'likes' singular?
options: The sentence is in past tense
questions.explanation: Valli is a singular subject, so it takes the singular verb 'likes'.

questions.question: Two or more subjects joined by 'and' take:
questions.explanation: Rule 1 states that two or more subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Sunil, Renu, Medha and I is good friends.
Sunil, Renu, Medha and I are good friends.
Sunil, Renu, Medha and I am good friends.
Sunil, Renu, Medha and I was good friends.
questions.explanation: Multiple subjects joined by 'and' take the plural verb 'are'.

questions.question: Bread, butter and jam ______ common breakfast items.
questions.explanation: The compound subject 'Bread, butter and jam' is plural, so it takes 'are'.

questions.question: Which rule applies to 'Professor Jaya Shekar and Professor Maya Patkar are doing a combined project'?
options: Titles of books take singular verbs.
Pair of takes a singular verb.
Two subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb.
questions.explanation: The two professors are joined by 'and', so the plural verb 'are' is used.

questions.question: Anusha and her sisters ______ at university.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb, so 'are' is correct.

questions.question: In 'The noise of the chirping crickets was a constant feature,' why is the verb 'was' singular?
options: The subject is 'crickets,' which is plural.
The subject is 'noise,' which is singular.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'noise', not 'crickets'. The phrase 'of the chirping crickets' is extra information, so the singular verb 'was' agrees with 'noise'.

questions.question: The list of invitees ______ ready.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'list', which is singular; 'of invitees' is an intervening phrase.

questions.question: All his mother's hopes ______ on his shoulders.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'hopes', which is plural, so the plural verb 'rest' is correct.

questions.question: What should you do when the subject and verb are separated by several other words?
options: Identify the actual subject and make the verb agree with it.
Make the verb agree with the nearest noun.
questions.explanation: Rule 2 states that in such cases, you should identify the subject and verb correctly.

questions.question: A collective noun thought of as a single unit takes:
questions.explanation: Rule 3 states that collective nouns thought of as a single unit take a singular verb.

questions.question: A team of expert lawyers ______ investigating the case.
questions.explanation: 'A team' is a collective noun thought of as a single unit, so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: The committee ______ agreed to meet next Wednesday.
questions.explanation: 'The committee' is a collective noun acting as a single unit, so it takes 'has'.

questions.question: When members of a collective noun are thought of as individual units, the verb is:
questions.explanation: Rule 4 states that when members of a collective noun are thought of as individual units, it takes a plural verb.

questions.question: The jury ______ divided in their opinion about the guilty verdict.
questions.explanation: The members of the jury are thought of as individual persons, so the plural verb 'were' is used.

questions.question: Subjects with 'pair of' take:
questions.explanation: Rule 5 states that subjects with the phrase 'pair of' take a singular verb because 'pair' refers to one thing.

questions.question: A pair of jeans ______ all that he bought from the shop.
questions.explanation: 'A pair of jeans' is treated as a single unit, so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: A pair of scissors ______ needed to cut the ribbon.
questions.explanation: 'A pair of scissors' is treated as a single unit, so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Where ______ my new pair of spectacles?
questions.explanation: 'A pair of spectacles' is singular in this context, so 'is' is correct.

questions.question: Two singular nouns joined by 'or' take:
questions.explanation: Rule 6 states that two singular nouns joined by 'or' take a singular verb.

questions.question: Mary or John ______ going to escort the chief guest.
questions.explanation: Two singular nouns joined by 'or' take a singular verb, so 'is' is correct.

questions.question: Neither Janani nor Jatin ______ ready with the presentation.
questions.explanation: Two singular nouns joined by 'neither...nor' take a singular verb.

questions.question: When two or more nouns are joined by correlative conjunctions, the verb agrees with:
options: The noun or pronoun closest to it
questions.explanation: Rule 7 states that the verb agrees with the noun or pronoun placed closest to it.

questions.question: Either my friends or my brother ______ going to book the tickets.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the nearest noun 'brother', which is singular, so 'is' is correct.

questions.question: Either my brother or my friends ______ coming to pick me up from the station.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the nearest noun 'friends', which is plural, so 'are' is correct.

questions.question: Neither the director nor the actor ______ patient or reasonable.
questions.explanation: Two singular nouns joined by 'neither...nor' take a singular verb, so 'was' is correct.

questions.question: Either Dhoni or Kohli ______ going to captain the team tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Two singular nouns joined by 'either...or' take a singular verb.

questions.question: Neither my brother nor my parents ______ about my grade card.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the nearest noun 'parents', which is plural, so 'know' is correct.

questions.question: Indefinite pronouns such as 'everything' and 'nothing' usually take:
questions.explanation: Rule 8 states that indefinite pronouns such as much, many, anything, nothing, everything, something, either and neither usually take a singular verb.

questions.question: Neither of the two houses ______ a balcony.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is an indefinite pronoun that takes a singular verb, so 'has' is correct.

questions.question: Everything ______ very expensive these days.
questions.explanation: 'Everything' is an indefinite pronoun that takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Much money ______ been spent on renovating the house.
questions.explanation: 'Much' is an indefinite pronoun that takes a singular verb, so 'has' is correct.

questions.question: Nothing ______ worth losing sleep over.
questions.explanation: 'Nothing' is an indefinite pronoun that takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Singular subjects followed by 'as well as,' 'along with,' and 'besides' take:
questions.explanation: Rule 9 states that singular subjects followed by these words take a singular verb.
questions.topic: As well as / Along with / Besides

questions.question: The teacher, along with her students, ______ down to watch a film.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'teacher' (singular), and 'along with her students' does not change the agreement, so 'sits' is correct.
questions.topic: As well as / Along with / Besides

questions.question: A good book as well as the company of friends ______ her happy.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'book' (singular), so the singular verb 'makes' is correct.
questions.topic: As well as / Along with / Besides

questions.question: The dolphins, along with the orca, ______ together in the ocean.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'dolphins' (plural), so the plural verb 'are swimming' is correct.
questions.topic: As well as / Along with / Besides

questions.question: Distances, periods of time and sums of money, when considered as a single unit, take:
questions.explanation: Rule 10 states that distances, periods of time, and sums of money considered as a single unit take a singular verb.

questions.question: Ten miles ______ a long distance to walk.
questions.explanation: 'Ten miles' is considered a single unit, so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Five years ______ a long time to not meet your friends.
questions.explanation: 'Five years' is considered a single period of time, so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Ten thousand dollars ______ the prize money offered in the game show.
questions.explanation: 'Ten thousand dollars' is a sum of money considered as a single unit, so it takes 'is'.

questions.question: Words like 'all,' 'none,' 'some,' and 'most' take a singular verb when:
options: The verb is in past tense
questions.explanation: Rule 11 states that these words take a singular verb when the subject is singular and a plural verb when the subject is plural.

questions.question: Most of the pie ______ already been eaten.
questions.explanation: The subject 'pie' is singular, so 'most of the pie' takes the singular verb 'has'.

questions.question: Some of the jury members ______ in a meeting right now.
questions.explanation: The subject 'jury members' is plural, so 'some of the jury members' takes the plural verb 'are'.

questions.question: Titles of books always take:
questions.explanation: Rule 12 states that titles of books always take a singular verb even if the name has plural nouns.

questions.question: American Gods ______ a book by Neil Gaiman that has been adapted for television.
questions.explanation: The title of the book 'American Gods' is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'is'.
